userStories.title: Move the session lock layer into nax-agent with neutral errors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the existing ownership and mutation-guard protocol to nax-agent with neutral NaxError refusals and one shared freshness predicate.

**Motivation** — The moved code must not pull the ACP SDK into nax-agent.

**Approach** — Relevant design text, verbatim:

**Error contract.** Every refusal of `acquireLock` (a fresh lock held by another
live pid, a takeover that loses a race, and guard contention) is a `NaxError`
with code `SESSION_LOCKED`, the same message text as today
(`session in use by pid <pid>` or `session in use by another process`), and
context `{ stage: "session-store" }` plus `pid` when known.
`SessionLockGuardBusy` becomes a `NaxError` subclass with code `SESSION_LOCKED`
and message `session in use by another process`, still distinguishable with
`instanceof` by the release retry loop. An invalid list cursor is a `NaxError`
with code `SESSION_LIST_CURSOR_INVALID`, message `invalid cursor`.
`SESSION_META_UNREADABLE` keeps its code and message; its context `stage`
becomes `"session-store"`.

The freshness check is one
predicate exported from `session-lock.ts` (not from the package entry),
`holderState(body, deps, isAlive): SessionLockHolderState`, created in US-001,
that both `takeover` and `readLockHolder` call, so the two cannot drift; `takeover` refuses exactly when it returns
`"live"`.

**Ported tests (US-001, US-002).** The moved tests replace the ACP-only
`#test/helpers/recording-logger` (`lines`) with nax-agent's `makeLogger()` from
`test/helpers/agent-logger.ts` (`calls`). The moved fixture
`test/fixtures/session-store/lock-contender.ts` imports
`#src/session-store/session-lock` and `#src/session-store/session-lock-guard`
and passes an inline no-op `AgentLogger` (it runs as a child `bun` process, not
under `bun test`); the hardening test spawns it as
`join(import.meta.dir, "../../fixtures/session-store/lock-contender.ts")`.

Implementation allocation: create only src/session-store/session-lock.ts, session-lock-guard.ts and the two ported test/fixture outputs in this story. Unless an acceptance criterion explicitly advances the clock, direct lock/predicate tests use deps.pid 1000 and deps.now fixed at 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z. The child fixture retains its independent process identity and deliberately later clock to attempt stale takeover at the parent's mutation barrier. Declare SessionStorageDeps and the internal SessionLockHolderState union in session-lock.ts, avoiding any dependency on storage.ts. Extract holderState from the existing takeover condition: return own for deps.pid first (even if isAlive says dead), live for another alive pid with no heartbeat or heartbeat age <= LOCK_STALE_MS, and stale otherwise. Retain the modern/legacy lock schema, fully written exclusive link, guard markers, race restoration, nonce ownership, heartbeat and instanceof-based release-retry logic. Keep info/warn logger stages session; only NaxError context uses session-store. Port storage-hardening.test.ts to call acquireSessionLock directly; do not depend on the facade US-002 creates. Preserve the existing hardening cases and real separate-process mutation barrier. Regression tests must fail against the old code before implementation; follow strict three-session TDD.

**Scope** — In: lock implementation, guard, internal freshness predicate, lock dependency type, direct hardening test port and child fixture. Out: metadata/listing/facade and package exports (US-002), readLockHolder and public holder exports (US-003), ACP import/error mapping and removal of originals (US-004). This story adds new files only, modifies no existing assertions or package entry, and leaves ACP copies intact. The on-disk formats do not change: `<id>.session.json` stays `schemaVersion: 1` with the same fields, `<id>.lock` keeps its body shape (nonce plus heartbeat, and legacy pid-only locks), and file names and the temp-then-rename write stay as they are. These lock behaviours move unchanged and are covered by the ported `storage-hardening.test.ts` cases, not by new acceptance criteria: the heartbeat stops once the lock file names another nonce, takeover restores a renamed file that changed under it and refuses, dead mutation guards are reaped, a crash inside the guard leaves it reapable, and release retries on `SessionLockGuardBusy` (still matched by `instanceof`) until it can check the nonce. Lock semantics are moved, not redesigned: no new concurrency guarantee, no change to the heartbeat interval or stale threshold, no network-filesystem or Windows support work.

**Interface** — Verbatim target contract notes:

`session-lock.ts` — Baseline: `acquireSessionLock(path, deps: StorageDeps, isAlive)`;
`refused(pid?)` returns `RequestError.invalidRequest(...)`. Target: same signature
with `SessionStorageDeps`; `refused(pid?)` returns
`new NaxError(message, "SESSION_LOCKED", { stage: "session-store", ...(pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {}) })`
with the unchanged message. `LOCK_HEARTBEAT_MS = 30_000` and `LOCK_STALE_MS = 120_000`
are unchanged and exported.

`session-lock-guard.ts` — Baseline: `class SessionLockGuardBusy extends RequestError`
(`-32600`). Target: `class SessionLockGuardBusy extends NaxError`, code
`SESSION_LOCKED`, message `session in use by another process`.

```typescript
export interface SessionStorageDeps {
  readonly dir: string;
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly now: () => Date;
  readonly logger: AgentLogger;
  readonly setInterval?: (callback: () => void, ms: number) => ReturnType<typeof setInterval>;
  readonly isAlive?: (pid: number) => boolean;
}
export type SessionLockHolderState = "live" | "stale" | "own";
```

The internal acquireSessionLock callable remains `(path: string, deps: SessionStorageDeps, isAlive: (pid: number) => boolean) => () => Promise<void>`. The listed neutral type is internal until its public re-export in the dependent stories; holderState is never exported from the package entry.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Given deps.pid 1000, deps.now fixed at 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, and a lock { pid: 4242, startedAt, nonce, heartbeatAt: '2026-10-09T00:00:00.000Z' } whose pid is alive, acquireSessionLock(path, deps, isAlive) throws a NaxError with code SESSION_LOCKED.
[unit] Given that fresh live-pid lock refusal, the error message contains 'session in use by pid 4242'.
[unit] Given that fresh live-pid lock refusal, the error context.pid is 4242.
[unit] When acquireSessionLock refuses a fresh lock held by another live pid, the lock file bytes remain unchanged.
[unit] Given deps.pid 1000 and now 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, acquireSessionLock over live pid 4242 with heartbeatAt one millisecond more than LOCK_STALE_MS before now returns a release function.
[unit] After that stale-heartbeat takeover, the lock file's pid is 1000.
[unit] When that stale lock is taken over, the logger emits an info with message 'taking over a stale session lock', preserving the existing behavior.
[unit] Given a lock held by a dead pid, acquireSessionLock returns a release function, preserving stale takeover behavior.
[unit] Given a lock held by a dead pid, stale takeover emits an info with message 'taking over a stale session lock', preserving the existing behavior.
[unit] Given deps.pid 1000 and now 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, acquireSessionLock over a legacy { pid: 4242, startedAt } lock with no nonce or heartbeat and 4242 alive throws SESSION_LOCKED.
[unit] When the returned release function is called for its owned lock, the lock file is removed.
[unit] When the release function is called after the lock file was rewritten with a different nonce, the lock file remains in place holding that other nonce.
[unit] Given deps.setInterval stubbed to capture the heartbeat callback, acquireSessionLock calls it with LOCK_HEARTBEAT_MS, which is 30000.
[unit] Given the captured heartbeat callback and deps.now advanced from 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-09T00:00:30Z, invoking the callback rewrites heartbeatAt to '2026-10-09T00:00:30.000Z'.
[unit] new SessionLockGuardBusy() is an instance of NaxError.
[unit] new SessionLockGuardBusy() has code SESSION_LOCKED.
[unit] When another process holds the mutation guard, acquireSessionLock throws SessionLockGuardBusy with message 'session in use by another process'.
[unit] Given deps.pid 1000 and now 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, holderState for live pid 4242 with heartbeatAt exactly LOCK_STALE_MS before now returns 'live'.
[unit] Given deps.pid 1000 and now 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, holderState for pid 1000 returns 'own', even when isAlive reports 1000 dead.
[unit] Given deps.pid 1000 and now 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, holderState for pid 4242 that isAlive reports dead returns 'stale'.

[integration] While the parent process is inside a heartbeat lock mutation and its _lockDeps.rename barrier spawns the child, the child run from test/fixtures/session-store/lock-contender.ts against the same lock path prints { acquired: false }.
[integration] After the parent leaves that mutation, the same child run prints a result with acquired: true.
[integration] After that child takes ownership, the parent's later release leaves the child's nonce in the lock file.

routing.reasoning: Extracts concurrent filesystem ownership and guard/release behavior across modules with real-process race tests; session ownership invokes the security override and strict test isolation.

userStories.title: Add a read-only session lock-holder snapshot
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add SessionStorage.readLockHolder and public holder types so a host can display ownership without acquiring or mutating a session lock.

**Motivation** — A host cannot see who holds a lock.

**Approach** — Verbatim design:

**Lock-holder read (US-003).** `SessionStorage.readLockHolder(sessionId)` reads
`<id>.lock` without the guard and without writing, and classifies the holder with
the same freshness rule `takeover` uses to refuse: a holder is `"live"` when its
pid is not this storage's `pid`, `isAlive(pid)` is true, and it is either a
legacy lock (no heartbeat) or its `heartbeatAt` is no older than
`LOCK_STALE_MS`; `"own"` when its pid equals this storage's `pid`; otherwise
`"stale"`. A missing lock file, or a body the lock schema rejects, returns
`null`, because `acquireLock` would take such a file over. The result is a
snapshot; `acquireLock` stays the only authority. The freshness check is one
predicate exported from `session-lock.ts` (not from the package entry),
`holderState(body, deps, isAlive): SessionLockHolderState`, created in US-001,
that both `takeover` and `readLockHolder` call, so the two cannot drift; `takeover` refuses exactly when it returns
`"live"`.

Implementation allocation: extend the existing storage facade and its named barrel/root exports; return exactly pid, startedAt, heartbeatAt and state, using null for a legacy heartbeat and not exposing nonce. Reuse US-001's lock schema/read semantics and holderState; do not introduce a second freshness predicate or a dependency from session-lock.ts onto storage.ts. Make SessionLockHolder and SessionLockHolderState public and regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt with bun run api:update. Add test/unit/session-store/lock-holder.test.ts with the deterministic pid/time fixture; readLockHolder/acquireLock agreement tests operate on stable lock fixtures and release any acquired lock. Strict three-session TDD applies.

**Scope** — In: readLockHolder implementation, holder result/state types, named exports, snapshot update and behavioral tests. Out: redesigning the lock protocol (US-001), changing metadata or listing behavior (US-002), ACP wiring/deletions (US-004). US-003 only: readLockHolder is a point-in-time snapshot; the holder can change right after the read, and only acquireLock decides ownership. US-003 only: readLockHolder does not take the mutation guard, so a read during another process's lock rename may see no file and return null. No host/TUI implementation is added.

**Interface** — Verbatim holder declarations and additive method:

```typescript
export type SessionLockHolderState = "live" | "stale" | "own";
export interface SessionLockHolder {
  readonly pid: number;
  readonly startedAt: string;
  readonly heartbeatAt: string | null;
  readonly state: SessionLockHolderState;
}
```

```typescript
readLockHolder(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionLockHolder | null>; // US-003
```

The method is added to SessionStorage and the object returned by createSessionStorage. The shared internal predicate remains `holderState(body, deps, isAlive): SessionLockHolderState`, not a root export.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Given storage with pid 1000 and now fixed at 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z, readLockHolder(id) with no <id>.lock file resolves to null.

[unit] Given that storage and a lock { pid: 4242, startedAt, nonce, heartbeatAt: '2026-10-09T00:00:00.000Z' } with isAlive reporting 4242 alive, readLockHolder(id) resolves to { pid: 4242, startedAt, heartbeatAt: '2026-10-09T00:00:00.000Z', state: 'live' }.
[unit] Given that same lock with isAlive reporting 4242 dead, readLockHolder(id) resolves with state 'stale'.
[unit] Given that storage and a lock whose pid is 1000, readLockHolder(id) resolves with state 'own'.
[unit] Given that storage and a legacy { pid: 4242, startedAt } lock with 4242 alive, readLockHolder(id) resolves with heartbeatAt null and state 'live'.
[unit] Given that storage and a lock file holding 'not json', readLockHolder(id) resolves to null.
[unit] Given that storage and a lock file holding { pid: -1 }, readLockHolder(id) resolves to null.
[unit] After readLockHolder(id) over a live lock, the lock file bytes are unchanged.
[unit] After readLockHolder(id) over a live lock, the directory holds no new file.
[unit] When readLockHolder(id) reads a missing or schema-invalid lock file, directory contents and any existing lock file bytes remain unchanged, with nothing written or deleted.
[unit] For a stable lock readLockHolder reports as 'live', acquireLock on the same storage rejects with SESSION_LOCKED.
[unit] For a stable lock readLockHolder reports as 'stale', acquireLock on the same storage resolves.
[unit] For a stable lock readLockHolder reports as 'own', acquireLock on the same storage resolves.
[unit] After acquireLock resolves for that 'own' lock, the lock file holds a new nonce.

routing.reasoning: Adds one read-only facade capability using the existing schema and classifier, with export/snapshot changes; session ownership inspection invokes the security override.

analysis:
Goal and completion: implement F2 of the interactive coding agent slice 1 by relocating ACP metadata, ownership locks and listing into @nathapp/nax-agent, exposing neutral public types plus a read-only holder snapshot, then consuming that implementation from ACP without changing disk or JSON-RPC compatibility. The TUI and koda share only the machine-local session store; a TranscriptStore alone cannot supply ACP discovery. This is an existing-code extraction and enhancement, not a new persistence design.

Exploration: codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct file reads and text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax. The checked source agrees with the supplied baseline. Existing instructions are scoped by packages/nax-agent/AGENTS.md and packages/nax-agent-acp/AGENTS.md; no deeper AGENTS.md files were found. References below identify the current implementation, not a proposed replacement baseline.

Current metadata/listing architecture: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/storage.ts:8-15 imports node filesystem operations, ACP ListSessionsResponse/SessionInfo, ACP error helpers and server-local mode constants. storage.ts:19-37 defines SESSION_ID_PATTERN, LIST_PAGE_SIZE=50 and a Zod schemaVersion:1 metadata schema; storage.ts:39-57 defines SessionStorage and StorageDeps. storage.ts:66-73 implements processAlive with EPERM treated as alive. storage.ts:75-80 constructs SESSION_META_UNREADABLE with stage agent-server; only the error context stage changes to session-store. storage.ts:86-93 decodes offset cursors using Buffer, a digits check and Number.isSafeInteger; absent/null/empty cursors currently mean offset zero. Preserve existing cursor behavior rather than introducing unrelated canonical-base64 validation. storage.ts:95-97 supplies updatedAt ?? createdAt to listing entries. storage.ts:104-125 distinguishes missing metadata from invalid JSON, unsupported versions and bad shapes, without repairing files. storage.ts:133-162 scans only .session.json files, skips unreadable metadata with a session-stage warning, filters exact cwd, sorts descending by effective timestamp and pages by 50. storage.ts:168-175 creates the directory and atomically temp-writes then renames metadata; hasMeta/removeMeta are at storage.ts:177-185. Preserve their behavior, optional costUsd and existing field validation, including rejecting review as a persisted mode. The metadata schema must use BashApprovalModeSchema from packages/nax-agent/src/config/bash-approval.ts:12-14 rather than ACP's independent BASH_APPROVALS array. The shared schema and SESSION_META_MODES/SessionMetaMode/SESSION_ID_PATTERN/defaultSessionsDir belong in the new session-meta.ts; SessionListEntry and SessionListPage are transport-neutral.

Current ownership architecture and risk: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/session-lock.ts:10-27 defines the unchanged 30000ms heartbeat, 120000ms stale threshold and modern/legacy body schema. session-lock.ts:29-50 provides filesystem seams, tolerant reads, nonce/legacy comparison and ACP refusal construction. session-lock.ts:52-99 creates a fully written lock by linking a unique temp file, checks a holder before takeover, protects renamed files from races and logs stale takeover. session-lock.ts:68-73 is the existing freshness condition to extract into holderState; own pid takes precedence over liveness, exactly LOCK_STALE_MS old is still live, dead holders and older heartbeats are stale, and a live legacy pid remains live without an age test. session-lock.ts:101-116 retries release on instanceof SessionLockGuardBusy using an unref'ed delay; session-lock.ts:118-158 obtains the guard, creates nonce ownership, heartbeats under the guard, stops on ownership loss and clears the timer after release. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/session-lock-guard.ts:7-10 currently subclasses RequestError. session-lock-guard.ts:18-50 removes only its own marker, fails closed on unknown markers and reaps only proven ESRCH deaths; session-lock-guard.ts:54-77 atomically publishes a nonempty guard directory and always cleans its own marker. Move these algorithms rather than replacing them with a check-then-write lock. All lock refusals, including race loss and guard contention, become NaxError SESSION_LOCKED with the existing message and stage session-store, plus pid when known. SessionLockGuardBusy must remain a distinct subclass so release retries still function. The lock layer declares SessionStorageDeps itself (choose session-lock.ts to avoid an extra output and any dependency on storage.ts); it also owns the internal holder-state union needed by US-001. US-003 can re-export that same union publicly rather than creating a second definition. Shared lock-body reading/schema access must stay inside the session-store implementation so holder inspection cannot drift from takeover.

Holder snapshot: US-003 adds SessionStorage.readLockHolder, returning only pid, startedAt, heartbeatAt (null for legacy) and state; nonce is not exposed in this result. It reads without mkdir, guard acquisition, heartbeat, ownership mutation, repair or deletion. Missing/unparseable/schema-invalid bodies return null. It calls the very same holderState introduced in US-001 and used by takeover. Read/acquire agreement is tested with a stable fixture; the read is never an ownership guarantee and a concurrent rename can produce a null snapshot. Do not broaden this feature into a new concurrency protocol or infer a new filesystem-error policy beyond the specified cases.

Package API/boundaries: packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:1-8 requires explicit named exports and keeps underscore seams off the root entry; index.ts:87 already exports the NaxError class used by ACP. packages/nax-agent/src/infra/nax-error.ts:6-15 accepts arbitrary string codes and optional context, so no new error-code enum or class duplication is required. packages/nax-agent/src/infra/errors.ts:10-12 supplies errorMessage to replace ACP messageOf. packages/nax-agent/package.json:7-15 maps the root entry and #src/#test aliases; package.json:39-43 has Zod but no ACP SDK dependency. No new package subpath or dependency is needed. Add a named session-store barrel and named root re-exports; publish createSessionStorage, defaultSessionsDir, processAlive, LIST_PAGE_SIZE, LOCK_HEARTBEAT_MS, LOCK_STALE_MS, SESSION_ID_PATTERN, SESSION_META_MODES, SessionMeta, SessionMetaMode, SessionListEntry, SessionListPage, SessionStorage and SessionStorageDeps in US-002, then SessionLockHolder and SessionLockHolderState in US-003. holderState and acquireSessionLock remain deep implementation APIs, not root exports. Keep _lockDeps and guard helpers off the supported package entry; deep imports are only for nax-agent's own tests. Regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt with bun run api:update after each intended public addition, never hand-edit it. Use #src imports or explicit .ts relative filenames, Node-compatible source and the existing runtime/seam conventions.

ACP impact/dependents: text search found storage imports in packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/main.ts:28, connection.ts:15, registry.ts:36, registry-open.ts:15 and registry-lifecycle.ts:10, plus test/helpers/registry-setup.ts:8 and test/unit/server/{connection-sessions,registry-credentials,connection,connection-close-switch,registry-switch,connection-persistence}.test.ts. main.ts:116-124 already creates transcript and metadata stores over the same resolved directory; retain that wiring but import the storage constructor from @nathapp/nax-agent. connection.ts:45-65 wraps load/resume/list in guard, so registry-thrown NaxError reaches the protocol adapter without changing request routing. registry.ts:77-81 receives storage through RegistryDeps; registry.ts:197-200 takes the lock before opening; registry.ts:366 currently directly returns storage.list.
